studies.Reference: Postmenopausal Androgen Metabolism and Endometrial Cancer Risk in the Women's Health Initiative Observational Study.
studies.Authors: Michels KA, Brinton LA, Wentzensen N, Pan K, Chen C, Anderson GL, Pfeiffer RM, Xu X, Rohan TE, Trabert B
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: We measured prediagnostic serum concentrations of 12 androgens and their metabolites using highly sensitive liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry assays

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 313 endometrial cancer case subjects, 354 matched control subjects
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: dehydroepiandrosterone (5th vs 1st quintile: OR = 1.85, 95% CI = 1.06 to 3.25)
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: the highest levels of adrenal androgens were associated with increased endometrial cancer risk
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: Computed from the reported effect and 95% CI using a normal approximation: p=0.031.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: prediagnostic serum concentrations of 12 androgens and their metabolites
